news.title: Friday’s weather: More sunshine, high near 65
First Alert Forecast
news.og_title: First Alert Forecast
news.og_desc:
Quiet and dry conditions will continue as a strong high pressure system remains positioned over the Carolinas. An upper-level low pressure system along the Gulf Coast is expected to develop into a surface low near Florida on Friday, but this system will track northward along the Atlantic coastline and pose no threat to our region. The National Hurricane Center is monitoring this system for potential tropical cyclone development with a 60 percent probability, but again, no impacts are expected in our forecast area. Saturday will remain dry with partly sunny skies and afternoon highs reaching the mid 70s.
A weakening shortwave trough is expected to move through our area Sunday into Monday. While rain chances remain low at 20 to 30 percent, the trough and its associated cold front could squeeze out some moisture in the form of showers. Any rainfall that does occur will be light, with totals generally between 0.10 to 0.25 inches.
The latest U.S. Drought Monitor continues to show severe to exceptional drought conditions.  With the lack of significant rainfall in the forecast, drought conditions are expected to worsen through the middle of the week.
